subject: alebrije
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: alebrije jaguar-eagle.
Style: Oaxacan alebrije painted wood.
reasoning:
I'm designing an alebrije jaguar-eagle hybrid — a jaguar body and head combined with eagle wings, talons, and tail feathers — and planning the vivid Oaxacan-style painted patterns of dots, lines, and zigzags to decorate it.

For structure, I'm sketching a skeleton with hip-rooted spine, head/jaw joints, a tail chain, four IK legs, and wing chains with feather cards extending outward, plus an eagle-style tail fan.

For the surface, I'm planning distinct paint treatments per body part — an orange-red base with yellow/teal dots for the body, blue with white dots for the wings — using cell-based dot patterns, alongside eye and face decal textures to finish the look.

I decide on a jaguar head with fangs and an eagle-feather crest/ruff rather than mixing in a beak, pairing jaguar legs and paws with eagle wings and a feathered tail fan for a clear chimera silhouette. Now I'm sketching out the builder API calls I'll need — joints, chains, sweeps/lofts, and limb helpers — to construct this in code.

Mapping out more SDK functions...

Now I'm working out the body loft stations from rump to chest, assigning the spine chain as the bone reference since the hips joint itself owns no loft segment, and starting to plan the tail chain as a catmull curve.

For the tail I'm sketching five joints curving backward and upward from the rump, parented to hips with a tapering sweep radius, then moving on to the eagle's fan of tail feathers arranged as a ring at the rump, using a frame oriented upward and figuring out the angular range so the feathers spread backward rather than forward.

I'm working through how to orient each feather card so it faces outward along the ring's radial direction rather than defaulting to a forward-facing flow, since the usual flow vector gets awkward for an upward-pointing axis -- leaning toward just setting flow to point straight up to keep the cards oriented sensibly.

Now I'm positioning the jaguar's tail to curve upward so it clears the feather fan sitting below it, then moving on to leg placement -- setting shoulder and foot coordinates for the forelegs with the elbow bending backward in typical feline fashion.

For the hind legs I'm mirroring that logic with knees bending forward instead, chaining shoulder-elbow-wrist joints down to the paws, and sweeping the limb geometry with tapering radii. For the paws themselves, I'm considering whether to use a toe-ring generator or just place four individual toe spheres plus talon cones manually, since the eagle-like foot needs distinct claws.

Now I'm defining the wing skeleton with shoulder, elbow, wrist, and tip points spreading outward and slightly downward, then sweeping tapered bone radii along that chain. For feathers, I'm planning to use an iteration helper along the wrist-to-tip and elbow-to-wrist segments to extrude individual primary and secondary feather shapes.

I should compute the perpendicular manually rather than trust automatic orthogonalization, writing a helper to project out the component along x. For the feather shape itself, I'm defining a tapered outline centered on the midline with smoothing, parameterized by length and width so each feather can scale independently -- and considering whether textured cards might work better than geometric outlines.

Carved-plank style feels more authentic, so I'll extrude the feathers with a paint function that stripes colors along the outline coordinate to mimic painted wood. For layout I'm planning roughly seven primaries and six secondaries per side, plus a shorter row of coverts offset slightly on top in a different color, totaling around forty feather pieces -- skipping a wing membrane since the feathers alone should read well. Now I'm moving on to the head, starting with a scaled skull sphere at the neck.

Beyond the skull I'm sketching out the muzzle box, separate upper and lower jaw bones with the lower one jointed for articulation, ears as lathed shapes or cones, decal-based eyes, a small nose box, cone fangs, thin whisker rods, and a crest of feather cards along the back of the head. For the eye decal I want that bold alebrije look -- concentric white, orange, and black rings with highlights and a dotted lid -- and for surface patterns I'm designing paint functions for dots and wavy stripe lines keyed to cell distance and id.

Now I'm working out jaguar-style rosette patterns for the body paint -- rings of dots computed by angle and radius around a center point -- plus a cream countershaded belly with fine dots, and a blue wing pattern with white dots and a yellow stripe.

For the legs I'll reuse the body paint, and for the tail I'll alternate banded colors with dots along the sweep. I'm settling on a magenta, orange, yellow, teal, blue, purple, lime, cream, black, white, red palette to keep the flat color count under 64, and I want dot density high enough that each dot reads clearly at real-world scale, so I'll bump the paint texture to 2048. I'm also considering whether this alebrije figure needs a base at all.

Importing the builder utilities and planning out helper functions for painting dotted patterns onto surfaces, confirming which math exports are available for use.

Writing dotted and rosette paint functions...

Since side surfaces project the dot pattern into angular bands, I decide to select which two axes to use based on which normal component dominates. Then I sketch the body paint logic: belly region gets flat color when facing downward, otherwise a rosette pattern, with a thin white dividing line at the transition for a clean cartoonish look. Now I'm moving to the wing feather paint, keying it off the position along the feather's length.

Since each feather has a different length, I decide to create the paint as a function of that length via closure rather than using a normalized fraction, since the position coordinate is in meters. I'm planning the color bands along the feather: blue with dots near the root, a yellow zigzag band partway along, magenta with white dots in the middle region, and nothing at the very tip.

With the band pattern settled, I'm now sketching the full build: setting up metadata, creating the builder, defining a palette, and starting the skeleton with a hip joint using a spine role.

Building the spine chain next...

Still writing body loft...

Still building head geometry...

For the ears I'll stick a teal cone with a smaller magenta cone inside onto the skin surface rather than placing raw geometry. Then for the crest, I'm arranging a ring of feather-textured cards radiating outward from the back of the head, tilted and angled to fan out like eagle plumage.

Next I need whiskers as rods from the muzzle, legs with sphere-based paws and toe/talon details as planned, and wings with a covert sweep along the arm bone plus a shoulder epaulette detail.

For the tail, I'll chain sweep bands with a tuft of cards or cone clusters at the end, plus a fan ring behind it. I'm also adding a dorsal row of small spike cones along the spine using the body sweep line, keeping the spikes positioned between the shoulders and tail so they don't collide with the wing attachment points.

I also want a forehead sun emblem decal on the skull, bringing the texture list to around four or five: eye, feather card, sun emblem, and tail feather card. I'm considering giving the eye decal a slight glow effect, then starting to write a helper function to generate feather outline points for extrusion.

Working out the feather orientation vectors...

Writing feather coloring logic...

Now I'm planning the covert feather coloring and the tail fan structure, using a ring of feather-textured cards arranged outward with a slight downward tilt, noting that joints requires a name parameter.

Setting up the tail bone chain with a curved spline going back and up from the hips, tapering the sweep radius along the way.

For color, I'll alternate bands using paint values rather than plain color strings, since bands accept Paint inputs directly. I'm also placing a tuft at the tail tip with a cone cluster, keeping the fan cards at a height that avoids clashing with the tail start, and now I'm thinking through spikes down the back and a neck ruff for the eagle variant.

Setting up the ruff, I'll use a ring of feather-textured cards positioned around a point along the neck chain, leaning backward along a flow direction so they fan toward the head like real plumage, choosing a count and radius that reads as dense but not cluttered. Now I'm moving on to defining the leg paint.

For the legs I'll blend from body color into a purple-dotted sock texture near the feet, switching based on height with a thin white band marking the transition, then apply skull surface shading and sketch the eye as a layered SVG with a dark outer ring, cream mid-ring, and large pupil for a cartoonish focal point.

Writing SVG code...

I'll add a sun emblem with rays for the forehead, a small pink tongue box, and need to carefully structure the limb chain data — using Vector3 points returned by the limb function to build named joint paths like shoulder, elbow, and tip for the leg chains.

owest point sits above the floor, so I'll lower the foot target to y=0.05 and adjust the paw scale so its bottom touches 0. Then I'm adding toe spheres spread across the front of the paw with small talon cones, and working out the wing's shoulder attachment point relative to the spine joints.

Parenting the wing to the chest makes sense here. I'm laying out the wing chain with shoulder, elbow, wrist, and tip points sweeping outward and slightly downward, keeping the root tucked inside the body width, then adding a shoulder plate disc with a sun decal positioned on the body surface.

The shoulder plate position looks fine against the wing root without clashing. I'm now working through the chain and extrude helper APIs, confirming how frames, bones, and perpendicular vectors are passed for feather placement, then starting a helper function to compute perpendicular directions for the feathers.

Writing body paint rules...

Finishing the angle-based ring test, then moving to the module setup, where I need to pin down the outline point type for the export.
